ci.method: PR #24's CI run 43794815103 on 56caddd, job sway (one of main's 19 required checks): a headless sway 1.9 of the tests' own on ubuntu-24.04, with CHATMON_SWAY=1 making a missing piece a failure, ran tests/test_sway.py and tests/test_wayland.py: 54 passed, 3 skipped. The overlay mapped as a layer surface sway draws and keeps out of its windows; clicks, the keyboard, the penguin's menu, the clipboard, full-screen windows, a screen going and drags all worked; buffers were the size of what is shown at 3840x2160 scale 2 and 2560x1440 scale 1.5; with a screen reader the ask box was a window sway floats, centres and focuses, and AT-SPI's registry found its field, buttons and conversation. The three skips say why: wlr-protocols isn't installed (the virtual pointer's opcode check), and Orca isn't installed (the two real-Orca tests, which ran in WSL: W5B-BEH-WSL-SWAY).

tests/test_sway.py and tests/test_wayland.py on their own in WSL, verbose, on 56caddd's files with the real sway 1.12, at-spi2-core 2.62.1 and Orca 51.1: 57 passed, none skipped, every real-compositor test by name, the two real-Orca tests among them (the ask box as a window announced and echoing typing; drawn on the overlay, neither announced nor echoed).

M3's memory.py on 56caddd's files: a headless sway at 3840x2160 and scale 2 with a window under the overlay, the overlay's buffers read inside Chatmon at each moment: at every moment at most two buffers, sized to what is shown (384x384, 640x640, 896x768, 896x1088), 1.1 to 7.4 MB, against fb19cb9's one or two full-output 3840x2160 buffers (31.6 to 63.3 MB) in M3's memory-before--window.json. With nothing showing, 5 s on, the overlay held 1 640x640 buffer (1.6 MB) and drew 0 frames in 2 s; that is within M3-04's at most two buffers sized to what is shown. The fb19cb9 side of the comparison is M3's own memory-before--window.json, whose code (revision 2's) hasn't changed.
